analysis.problem_summary: Relocate all zero values to the end of an array while maintaining the relative order of non-zero elements in-place.
analysis.intuition: Instead of shifting elements every time a zero is encountered, we can compress all non-zero elements toward the front using a write pointer. Once all non-zero elements are copied in order, every remaining array slot from the write pointer to the end must be filled with zero.
approach: Iterate through the array with a read pointer `i` from index 0 to `nums.length - 1`.
If `nums[i]` is non-zero, write `nums[i]` to `nums[j]` and increment `j`.
After completing the first pass, run a second loop from `j` to `nums.length - 1`, setting each position to 0.
analysis.why_it_works: Processing non-zero elements from left to right preserves their relative ordering. Because the write pointer `j` never advances faster than the read pointer `i`, non-zero values are safely copied forward without overwriting unread values. The second loop fills the remaining `n - j` trailing slots with zeroes.
analysis.key_takeaway: Decoupling array compaction into 'collecting non-zero elements' followed by 'filling zeroes' simplifies in-place array reordering without extra memory.
analysis.time_explanation: The array is traversed twice: first to copy non-zero elements, and second to fill zeroes. Both passes take linear time relative to the length of the array $n$, resulting in overall $O(n)$ time complexity.
analysis.space_explanation: The algorithm operates directly on the input array in-place using two integer pointer variables, requiring $O(1)$ auxiliary space.

analysis.problem_summary: Move all zeroes to the end of the array in-place while preserving the original relative order of non-zero elements in a single pass.
analysis.intuition: Maintain a write pointer `j` that tracks where the next non-zero element should be placed. As we scan the array, whenever we encounter a non-zero element at `i`, we move it to `j` and immediately clear position `i` to 0 (handling the case where `i == j` gracefully). This zeroes out old positions on the fly without a second loop.
approach: Iterate through the array with `i` from index 0 to `nums.length - 1`.
When `nums[i]` is non-zero, store its value, set `nums[i] = 0`, and assign the saved value to `nums[j]`.
Increment `j` after placing the non-zero element.
analysis.why_it_works: When `i == j` (before any zeroes are encountered), setting `nums[i] = 0` followed by `nums[j] = temp` leaves the element unchanged. When `i > j`, `nums[i]` was a non-zero value that gets moved to index `j`, leaving `nums[i]` correctly zeroed out. This maintains the invariant that all elements before `j` are non-zero and all elements between `j` and `i` are zeroes.
analysis.key_takeaway: Combining element placement and zeroing within a single iteration reduces total array write operations and eliminates the need for a post-processing fill loop.
analysis.time_explanation: The algorithm processes each element of the array exactly once in a single pass, performing $O(1)$ constant-time operations per element, giving an overall time complexity of $O(n)$.
analysis.space_explanation: The array is modified entirely in-place with a single extra index pointer `j` and a temporary scalar variable, taking $O(1)$ auxiliary space.
